hints: At constant speed, driving force equals resistance: $F = 480\text{ N}$.
Calculate power using $P = Fv = 480(24)$ and convert to kW.
walkthrough:
At constant speed ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$), the driving force equals resistance:
$$F = R = 480\text{ N}$$

Calculate power and convert to kW:
$$P = Fv = 480 \times 24 = 11520\text{ W} = 11.52\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Because the car moves at constant speed, acceleration is zero ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$), meaning the forward driving force $F$ balances the resistance force $R$:
$$F = R = 480\text{ N}$$

State the mechanical power formula:
$$P = Fv$$

Substitute $F = 480\text{ N}$ and $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 480 \times 24 = 11520\text{ W}$$

hints: Calculate the work done by the engine over 10 seconds: $W_{\text{engine}} = Pt = 12000(10) = 120000\text{ J}$.
Calculate the potential energy lost moving down the slope: $\Delta E_p = mg d\sin\theta = 1600(10)(280)(0.09) = 403200\text{ J}$.
Calculate the initial and final kinetic energies: $E_{k,i} = \frac{1}{2}(1600)(24^2) = 460800\text{ J}$ and $E_{k,f} = \frac{1}{2}(1600)(32^2) = 819200\text{ J}$.
Apply the work-energy balance: $W_{\text{engine}} + \Delta E_p - \Delta E_k = W_R$, giving $W_R = 164800\text{ J} = 164.8\text{ kJ}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total work done by the engine over the 10-second interval:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = Pt = 12000 \times 10 = 120000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the potential energy lost as the car descends the slope:
$$\Delta E_p = mg d\sin\theta = 1600(10)(280)(0.09) = 403200\text{ J}$$

Calculate the initial and final kinetic energies:
$$E_{k,i} = \frac{1}{2}(1600)(24^2) = 460800\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k,f} = \frac{1}{2}(1600)(32^2) = 819200\text{ J}$$
$$\Delta E_k = 819200 - 460800 = 358400\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle to find the work done against resistance $W_R$:
$$W_{\text{engine}} + \Delta E_p - W_R = \Delta E_k$$
$$120000 + 403200 - W_R = 358400$$
$$523200 - W_R = 358400 \implies W_R = 523200 - 358400 = 164800\text{ J}\quad (164.8\text{ kJ})$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work–Energy Principle: Finds engine work = 120000 J, PE lost = 403200 J, initial KE = 460800 J, final KE = 819200 J, and determines work against resistance = 164800 J (164.8 kJ).

teacher_walkthrough:
Name the work-energy theorem: the work input from the engine plus the potential energy lost down the slope equals the increase in kinetic energy plus the work done against resistive forces:
$$W_{\text{engine}} + \Delta E_p = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{resistance}}$$

Calculate the work supplied by the engine working at $12\text{ kW}$ for $10\text{ s}$:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = P \times t = 12000 \times 10 = 120000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the loss of gravitational potential energy along the $280\text{ m}$ descent with $\sin\theta = 0.09$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgd\sin\theta = (1600)(10)(280)(0.09) = 403200\text{ J}$$

Calculate the initial kinetic energy at $u = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,i} = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(1600)(24^2) = 800 \times 576 = 460800\text{ J}$$

Calculate the final kinetic energy at $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,f} = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(1600)(32^2) = 800 \times 1024 = 819200\text{ J}$$

Determine the kinetic energy gain:
$$\Delta E_k = 819200 - 460800 = 358400\text{ J}$$

Rearrange the work-energy equation to solve for $W_{\text{resistance}}$:
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = W_{\text{engine}} + \Delta E_p - \Delta E_k$$
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = 120000 + 403200 - 358400 = 523200 - 358400 = 164800\text{ J}$$
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = 164.8\text{ kJ}$$
